subject: New in MOPA Laser Rasterizer: build bigger, shape deeper, and control more
preheader: LightBurn browser integration, 800-cell Material Tests, Panel Tiling, Depthmap exports, and new artwork tools.
heading: Build bigger, shape deeper, and control more
intro: This release adds Chrome/Edge integration with local LightBurn, expands familiar engraving workflows, and introduces new tools for layered and geometric artwork.
highlights: Connect Rasterizer to local LightBurn with the Chrome/Edge browser extension beta, requiring LightBurn 2.23 or later. Import Material Library settings into Color or Processing palettes; imported settings are snapshots, not live synchronization.
Load native .lbrn2 files up to 250 MiB from Job History into LightBurn after reviewing and confirming project replacement. The extension does not start the laser.
Panel Tiling splits large designs across repeatable blanks and provides centered tile files, an assembly map, and a manifest.
Color Discovery can export native LightBurn Material Test presets with up to 800 cells, avoiding the 30-cell limit of color-layer-based project grids.
Expanded geometry tools add Halftone Newsprint, custom Glyph and Krasnow cells, tighter packing, seeded rotation, per-swatch routing, and source-image detail in Parallax SVG exports.

Depthmaps export as editable LightBurn Grayscale or Galvo 3D Sliced projects. Processing Palettes organize material settings by operation, including Cut, Score, Photo, Fill, Shovel, Cleaning, and 3D-Slice.
Layered Relief creates aligned physical layers with adjustable depth groups, per-layer and full-stack previews, registration features, score guides, and optional surface engraving.
Layered Mandala Lab creates coordinated multi-sheet radial artwork with custom motifs, openwork, structural supports, and per-layer Randomize and Reset controls.

SpiralGraph Lab creates open-line or filled-ribbon drawings from resizable tracks, gears, pencil reaches, and custom SVG or raster-image tracks, with independent drawing sizes and optional per-drawing palette routing.
Everyday workflow improvements include Job History thumbnails, steadier signed-in navigation, recoverable expired guest links, bulk swatch routing controls, and optional white engraving.
closing: These tools create editable starting points rather than machine-certified jobs. Inspect every generated LightBurn project and test on suitable scrap before running valuable work.
